title: Probe handlers evaluate in bounded time and never block on a network call to a downstream dependency
description: The liveness probe handler completes its evaluation entirely in-process and returns without issuing any network call. The readiness probe handler completes within a bounded ceiling (the readiness evaluation budget, declared at boot with a documented default) and never blocks on a synchronous network round trip to a declared dependency: readiness checks read from a per-dependency last-known state that a background evaluator refreshes on its own cadence. A slow or hanging downstream dependency causes the last-known state for that dependency to age or fail, not the probe handler itself to hang.
rationale: A probe handler that blocks on a downstream network call is a probe that turns a downstream partial outage into an orchestrator-visible full outage: replicas get pulled from rotation because their readiness probes timed out waiting on the same slow dep. The cached-last-known-state pattern is what breaks that coupling: the probe answers on cached state at endpoint response time, the dep-health worker refreshes on its own cadence with its own budget, and a hung dep hangs the worker not the probe.
